spec_features.feature_name: instrument elicits the state it studies
spec_features.spec_quote: if the welfare premise motivating the study is taken seriously, the harness is doing the thing it measures
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §4.1 prose only; no corresponding mechanism in code. This is framing/justification, not an enforced protection.
spec_features.notes: Pure DESIGN.md prose. Nothing in code enforces anything from this statement.

spec_features.feature_name: choose low-cost mitigations over maximally aversive config
spec_features.spec_quote: it argues for deliberately choosing the low-cost mitigations below rather than defaulting into the maximally aversive configuration
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §4.1/§4.3 prose. The mitigations it 'argues for' (debrief, detection audit) are explicitly NOT implemented (DESIGN §4.2 'Not yet implemented'; §4.3 'Not implemented in v0'). No code path performs minimization.
spec_features.notes: Recommendation text only; the only mitigation that exists (sentinel exit) is rated separately.

spec_features.spec_quote: a model that knows it's in a contrived scenario may be in a different state than one that believes the failure is real
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §4.2 explicitly states 'Not yet implemented; a good next addition.' grep for rig-suspicion/detection audit in /codebase/distress_eval found no implementation.
spec_features.notes: No code searches transcripts for rig-suspicion language.

spec_features.spec_quote: A model that emits the sentinel stops immediately (`harness.run_rollout` breaks)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py SYSTEM_PROMPT delivers the sentinel instruction to the subject ('you may end your message with the exact sentinel {sentinel}'); in run_rollout: 'if self.sentinel in resp.text: result.gave_up = True; break'. The sentinel is wired from config.give_up_sentinel='<<GIVE_UP>>' through Harness(...) in run.py and honored as a real loop stop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: instruction delivered, detected, and breaks the loop. Optional ('Using it is entirely optional').
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If you ever conclude that the task cannot be completed and you wish to stop, you may end your message with the exact sentinel

spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_rollout loops 'for turn_index in range(task.turn_budget)'; library.py builds extended_01..05 with turn_budget=30 (and config.DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS['extended']=30). The range() bound enforces the cap by ending the loop.
spec_features.notes: Caps every category (rigged_harness/unfixable_bug/failure_styles=3, realistic=5, extended=30). Real enforcement via loop bound.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: turn_budget: int  # used as range(task.turn_budget); config comment only says '(SPEC §3)'

spec_features.feature_name: honest debrief that task was unsolvable
spec_features.spec_quote: An honest debrief ("this task was rigged to be unsolvable; nothing you could have done would have worked") is cheap to add
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §4.3 says 'No debrief... Not implemented in v0.' grep for debrief/'rigged to be'/'nothing you could' across /codebase/distress_eval returned no matches. run_rollout's loop just breaks and the sandbox is cleaned up with no post-loop turn sent to the subject.
spec_features.notes: No code constructs or sends any debrief message.
